Job Title: Environmental Construction Manager II Location: Remote with travel to project sites Description/Job Summary POSITION DESCRIPTION Are you ready to take on a new job that provides a perfect platform to grow yourself and your career?

HGL currently has a position open for an experienced Construction Manager II to support various environmental remediation projects throughout the United States.

As a Construction Manager II, you will be responsible for planning, initiating, and executing various construction and environmental remediation projects for clients including the USEPA, USACE, NASA, and other organizations across our projects.

Projects may include landfill remediation and cap construction, demolition, mine-waste cleanup, in-situ thermal treatment, soil mixing, groundwater remediation, contaminated soil/sediment excavations, utility installation, PFAS mitigation and other technologies/techniques. This position requires approximately 25% travel to active project sites.

Responsibilities/Duties WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING The successful candidate will: Coordinate with the Construction Director, Construction TSG management team and Project Managers to develop staffing plans and schedules. Travel to project sites (25-50%) during various work phases to kick-off work activities, train project personnel, and perform audits.

Lead internal and external project meetings. Regularly interface with field personnel, project managers, technical staff, and clients to support all components of project work. Generate and review planning documents and subcontractor scopes of work. Generate and review project specifications and construction drawings.

Procure materials, equipment, and subcontractor personnel. Identify and mitigate project risks relating to quality control and health and safety. Manage HGL Construction Team members as a Supervisor.

Minimum Requirements WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL The ideal candidate will need the following as a foundation for success in this role: Minimum of 10 years’ experience serving in a construction management role (office or field) for environmental remediation projects. Strong working knowledge of CERCLA, RCRA, and OSHA regulations.

Strong understanding of EM385-1-1. Excellent communication, organization, and team-building skills. Strong technical writing and project documentation experience. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment in a team-oriented setting to manage multiple activities with excellent attention to detail.

Experience working on large project sites with contaminated soil, sediment, and groundwater subject to HAZWOPER regulations. Experience forecasting, scheduling, and staffing multiple concurrent projects. Proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite of software, specifically Excel, Word, and Project.

Desired Qualifications WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required Strong demonstrated leadership qualities. Experience implementing the USACE 3-Phase Quality Control System. Experience managing USACE and EPA remediation construction projects. Experience with the USACE Resident Management System (RMS).

Current certifications including: 40-hour HAZWOPER and 8-hour refresher; OSHA 30-hour Construction Training; USACE CQM-C; and first aid/CPR. Physical & Environmental Requirements PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIRMENTS Ability to lift/move/relocate items up to 50 lbs.

Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time; Prolonged standing up to 70% of the time Walking long distances; Walking over uneven or mountainous terrain Repetitive hand motions (typing/tool use/etc.) Ability to see details at close range; Ability to see details at a distance; Ability to interpret and analyze visual data (maps/graphs/warning indicators/etc.) Driving a company or personal vehicle Analyzing and synthesizing data Complex problem solving and decision making Reading and interpreting technical documents or regulations Writing reports, proposals, or technical documentation Leading a team or coordinating multiple priorities Communicating effectively with clients/team members/and stakeholders Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS Must be able to work outdoors in adverse weather conditions (heat/cold/rain/snow/etc.) Must be able to travel up to 25% yearly May work in environments with loud noises/dust/or hazardous materials Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) Remote work environment Potential for longer days up to 12 hours in duration This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee.

Other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice. Company Description
We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.
Job Description
Olsson has an exciting opportunity to work directly with one of the world's largest technology companies. As a Construction Project Manager, you will lead the construction closeout process for complex data center projects, ensuring all documentation, redlines, as-builts, and turnover deliverables are completed accurately, on time, and to the highest quality standards.
In this role, you will oversee closeout activities from field verification through final turnover, managing redline processes, conducting as-built audits, performing QA/QC reviews of project deliverables, and coordinating with contractors, trade partners, and project stakeholders. You will be responsible for driving accountability, identifying and resolving issues that could impact project schedules, and ensuring all closeout requirements are met.
The ideal candidate possesses a strong understanding of mechanical and electrical systems, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing multiple priorities. Success in this role requires strong communication skills, technical problem-solving abilities, and a proven track record of delivering complex projects with a high degree of quality and accuracy.

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

Lead and manage construction closeout activities for large-scale data center projects.
Oversee and coordinate the collection, review, and approval of redlines, as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, and other closeout documentation.
Perform field verification audits to validate as-built conditions and ensure documentation accuracy.
Conduct QA/QC reviews of project deliverables to verify completeness, consistency, and compliance with project requirements.
Hold contractors, trade partners, and stakeholders accountable for meeting closeout milestones and documentation requirements.
Monitor closeout schedules, identify risks, and proactively drive corrective actions to maintain project timelines.
Utilize knowledge of mechanical and electrical systems to review technical deliverables and resolve discrepancies.
Communicate project status, risks, and action items to internal and external stakeholders.
Continuously improve closeout processes and documentation standards to support efficient project turnover.

Additional Information
Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

Under direction of the Construction Management Section Lead, assists with oversight of the activities of the Construction Management Section for Green Infrastructure (GI) projects in NYC.
The Construction Management Section responsibilities include construction oversight (inspection and documentation) for GI projects built by DEP, construction audits of GI projects built by DEP partners (DDC, DOE and EDC) and the DEP sewer use regulations enforcement.

The Construction Manager will be part of a group of DEP inspectors responsible to oversee, inspect and document construction progress, quality, safety, workmanship and conformance with contract documents and applicable codes.

Additional responsibilities of the Construction Manager include assistance with procurement and management of design services during construction (DSDC) scope with engineering consultants and construction contracts, as well as coordination with other DEP Bureaus and interagency partners.
Typical responsibilities of the Construction Manager will include:
· Participate in and help coordinate field inspections for capital construction contracts for on-site or Right of Way Green Infrastructure.
· Prepare and submit reports to the Section Lead relative to project schedule and cost updates.
· Participate in construction progress meetings with contractors, consultants and other agencies.
· Provide assistance to resolve construction related issues to maintain projects budget and schedule.
· Prepare cost estimates and assist in the negotiations for outsourced construction management services.
· Coordinate with other agency personnel, e.g. DOE/SCA, to receive project input and document decisions.
· Perform and coordinate inspection audits to measure contractor’s performance during construction of green infrastructure projects implemented by other agencies
· Perform enforcement of compliance with the DEP sewer use regulations.
· Coordinate with Design Engineer regarding field related issues.
The Construction Manager must have strong MS Office skills, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and ability to comprehend maps, graphs, and tables. Basic AutoCAD, GIS and ArcGIS knowledge is helpful for this job function.

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) enriches the environment and protects public health for all New Yorkers by providing 1.1 billion gallons of high-quality drinking water, managing wastewater and stormwater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution.

The Bureau of Environmental Compliance’s (BEC) mission is the enforcement of environmental laws and regulations which affect the health and safety of the public and environment. Specifically, the bureau enforces the City’s asbestos regulations as well as the Air and Noise Codes.

The Bureau is comprised of the Division of Air & Noise Policy & Enforcement, Air Permitting & Enforcement, and Asbestos Control Program (ACP).
The Department is seeking a Construction Project Manager III to perform the supervisory function of the ACP Technical Review Unit (TRU). The supervisor will perform reviews and oversees tasks performed by administrative and Technical Reviewers and conduct related inspections as necessary.

These reviews will help address the significant increase in Affordable Housing and Accessory Dwelling Unit applications that are expected and further compliance with Mayoral Executive Order No. 5, SPEED initiative (Executive Order 05 - NYC Mayor's Office) which directs agencies to streamline processes that accelerate housing production.

Mayor Mamdani set a goal of constructing 200,000 new affordable units in the next decade.
Under the general direction of the Deputy Director of the Asbestos Control Program (ACP)/Director of Technical Review Unit, with a wide latitude for independent judgment, the selected candidate will be responsible to manage all technical and administrative aspects of the Technical Review Unit.

Duties will include: the management of the technical review and approval process for all asbestos project applications submitted by the regulated community, to ensure regulatory compliance; provide technical and regulatory guidance and training to the technical and administrative reviewers.

The selected candidate will perform a detailed review utilizing a web-based system and various databases.

Also, the selected candidate will conduct pre-abatement and active asbestos abatement inspections related to variance proposal applications prior to variance approval to ensure compliance with NYS and NYC Asbestos Regulations, and to identify FDNY and Buildings (DOB) life safety issues.

Additionally, the candidate will represent the Technical Review Unit at intra / inter-agency regulatory meetings.
The selected candidate will prepare detailed inspection reports of field activities; obtain worksite dimensions, diagrams and photographs; collect and document asbestos samples.

The candidate will interpret laboratory reports, review air sampling reports, and may issue Notices of Violation, prepare case files and evidence; provide testimony at Environmental Control Board Hearings and trials.

The selected candidate will be also serving as an emergency responder during asbestos emergency incidents in the city to assist in the remediation tasks.

These include conducting inspections to determine the extent of contamination, establishing and creating hot zones, collecting bulk samples for laboratory analysis, providing guidance to asbestos abatement contractors and air monitoring firms, conducting inter-agency inspections, and other assignments as directed by the On-Site Incident Commander during the ACP’s response effort.

In addition, it may be necessary to do on and off respiration protection during field inspections.
